bio: Data engineer with 4+ years across Genpact and Tata Consultancy Services delivering Amazon Redshift and Python-based ETL pipelines for large-scale industrial telemetry workloads. Currently at Genpact, I led the end-to-end redesign of a global industrial telemetry data pipeline, consolidating 37+ legacy stored procedures into 12 parameterized, config-driven ones, eliminating chronic deadlocks, and cutting backfill recovery from days to under 2 hours.

I'm comfortable owning a system from requirements through root-cause investigation, performance tuning, testing, and production handover. On the side I run a self-hosted Linux / Docker / Proxmox homelab, recently built a Databricks and PySpark pipeline on its data, and routinely use AI coding assistants (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, OpenCode) as a force multiplier on design, review, and automation work.

experience.summary: Data Optimization lead for the Amazon Redshift telemetry pipeline that loads 10-minute and 30-second data from thousands of sites worldwide.
highlights: Consolidated 37+ legacy stored procedures into 12 parameterized PL/pgSQL procedures, each handling daily loads and multi-year backfills through a single run_type parameter, with a config-driven model so a new data type is a single config-table insert.

Built a production-grade Python ETL orchestration framework (ThreadedConnectionPool + concurrent.futures) with dynamic worker auto-scaling, driving backfill recovery of 1 year of data from days to under 2 hours.

Redesigned a 3.5B-row join and a ~480M-row join that forced nested-loop execution on an OR predicate; pre-materialized equality lookup tables to enable hash joins, eliminating disk spill and converting both to single-pass execution.
Eliminated chronic production deadlocks by redesigning the lock strategy to hold staging-table locks only and adopting MERGE REMOVE DUPLICATES; zero lock-contention incidents post go-live.
Led a 3-day investigation into a watermark bug in a data-load procedure, identifying and recovering 23,784 systematically missing records.
Fixed a coverage dashboard reporting up to 200% coverage by rewriting the procedure against a unified, deduplicated view.
Expanded analytics coverage from 2 sites to all ~260+ streaming sites globally; removed site-level hardcoding so new sites onboard automatically.
Secured a data pipeline by replacing three uncoordinated cron scripts and a separate UDF with a single Python driver: pre-flight status checks, Fernet-encrypted credentials, and data-loss protection.
Authored and executed 216 parallel Prod-vs-QA test cases plus a 50-test mathematical validation of a schema migration; introduced GitHub source control to an engagement that previously had none.

projects.title: Amazon Redshift Pipeline Optimization
projects.description: End-to-end redesign and optimization of a global industrial telemetry pipeline on Amazon Redshift, ingesting 10-minute data from thousands of sites and synchronizing it into Redshift for operations, reporting, and analytics.

case.context: The pipeline had years of technical debt: chronic deadlocks, inconsistent deduplication across 37+ siloed stored procedures, sites hardcoded into UDF bodies, data gaps from legacy reject logic, ~260 sites missing from analytics, and manual backfills that took days to recover from a single outage.

metrics.label: Large-table joins
metrics.before: Nested loop on 3.5B rows, disk spill

deliverables.title: 12 Unified Parameterized Procedures
deliverables.body: Consolidated 37+ legacy stored procedures into 12 parameterized procedures. A single run_type parameter (daily, backfill, and variants) covers daily operations and multi-year backfills using the same validated transformation logic, with no divergence and no separate maintenance.

deliverables.title: Python ETL Orchestration Framework
deliverables.body: etl_workflow_final.py — a thread-safe RedshiftManager (psycopg2.ThreadedConnectionPool) + S3Manager + ETLWorkflow. Dynamic worker auto-scaling sizes the pool from the number of outstanding dates (capped at 25 for the WLM queue). Pre-checks stv_recents for Coreflow conflicts, processes dates in parallel via ThreadPoolExecutor, then bulk COPY FROM MANIFEST. Fully config-driven and dry-run capable.

deliverables.title: Large-Table Join Optimization
deliverables.body: A 3.5B-row join used an OR predicate, forcing a nested-loop join. Pre-materialized a union-based equality lookup table with aligned DISTKEY/SORTKEY, making the join hash-eligible and single-pass. Same fix applied to a ~480M-row join. Validated with EXCEPT in both directions: zero data difference.

deliverables.title: Deadlock & Lock-Strategy Redesign
deliverables.body: Legacy procedures locked the final table for the entire transformation. The new design locks only the staging table and adopts MERGE REMOVE DUPLICATES, dramatically reducing lock duration. Verified with live concurrency testing against svv_transactions / pg_locks — zero lock-contention incidents post go-live.

deliverables.title: Coverage Expansion & Duplicate Fix
deliverables.body: Expanded 30-second aggregation coverage from 2 sites to all ~260+ streaming sites, with a dedicated schema preventing signal mixing. Root-caused duplicate accumulation from upstream late-arrival timestamp updates; evaluated four approaches and adopted MERGE REMOVE DUPLICATES ("latest value as final value").

deliverables.title: Pipeline Update Script
deliverables.body: Replaced three uncoordinated cron scripts and a separate UDF with one Python driver. Adds a pre-flight check of the stored-procedure call log that blocks S3 re-upload if the prior run was aborted or stale (closing a real data-loss race), Fernet-encrypted credentials, and Prod→QA atomic sync.

deliverables.title: Log Monitor & Duplicate Alerting
deliverables.body: A log monitor verifies remote job completion purely from S3 (file age, failure-keyword scan, completion marker) with no SSH to the source host. KMS ARNs are regex-masked in logs. A consolidation procedure aggregates duplicate detection across all 7 sources and raises a ServiceNow incident when values genuinely conflict.

deliverables.title: Missing Records Investigation
deliverables.body: A 3-day structured investigation (snapshot → re-query Spectrum on the same watermark → dedup → EXCEPT) revealed that a data-load procedure's insert-timestamp watermark logic silently dropped records visible in source. Identified 23,784 missing records across statistic and channel categories; root cause fixed and validated.

projects.title: Serverless File Ingestion Pipeline: AWS Lambda, SQS, Redshift
projects.description: Owner of an event-driven AWS pipeline that ingests about 4,000 to 5,000 files (5 to 30 MB each) every 30 minutes: S3 event notifications trigger Lambdas that decrypt a proprietary file format, split it into five Parquet datasets and load them into Redshift with dedupe and merge. I set up Lambda monitoring, raised the load Lambda's success rate from 28% to 94% and a materialized view refresh from 10% to 100%.

case.context: Event-driven AWS pipeline. A file lands in S3 and an event notification triggers the first Lambda, which checks the file format and URI and sends the URI to an SQS queue. The queue triggers a second Lambda that decrypts the proprietary file format, splits it into five schemas and writes five Parquet files to a stage location and to the processed location. A third Lambda runs every 15 minutes: it takes stage files written before the current window, appends metadata from Athena, dedupes and merges them into Redshift, and clears them from the stage. A materialized view in Redshift refreshes every hour. The first two Lambdas are invoked about 4,000 to 5,000 times per 30 minutes, on files of 5 to 30 MB. I took the pipeline over after handover and knowledge transfer.

metrics.label: Refresh deadlocks
metrics.before: A timed-out run collided with the next run's refresh

deliverables.title: Pipeline architecture
deliverables.body: File lands in S3, an event notification triggers Lambda 1, which checks the format and URI and queues the URI in SQS. The queue triggers Lambda 2, which decrypts the file, separates five schemas and writes five Parquet files to stage and processed. Lambda 3 loads the stage into Redshift every 15 minutes, and a materialized view refreshes every hour.

deliverables.title: Ownership and monitoring
deliverables.body: Took ownership after handover and knowledge transfer. Set up monitoring that checks the ingest and processing Lambdas are being invoked, plus failure monitoring for the load Lambda.

deliverables.title: Load Lambda reliability
deliverables.body: The load Lambda runs every 15 minutes, takes only stage files written before the current window, appends Athena metadata, dedupes and merges into Redshift, then clears the stage. Its success rate went from 28% to 94%. It used to refresh the materialized view as its last step, and when a run hit the 15-minute Lambda limit, the next run's refresh could deadlock with the one still running.

deliverables.title: Materialized view optimization
deliverables.body: Optimized the materialized view definition, taking its refresh success rate from 10% to 100%. The refresh now runs on an hourly Redshift schedule instead of as the last step of the Lambda.

projects.title: Homelab Data Platform: Databricks & PySpark
projects.description: A bronze, silver and gold pipeline on Databricks and PySpark, built from the metrics my own Raspberry Pi and Proxmox homelab produce. Prometheus history is extracted in an LXC, landed in a Unity Catalog Volume, loaded with Auto Loader, cleaned with PySpark and served by SQL stored procedures to an AI/BI dashboard. A scheduler wakes the hardware only when the data is stale.

case.context: I had never used Databricks or PySpark. I wanted hands-on experience with the bronze, silver and gold pattern, so I built it on data I already had: the metrics from my own homelab. Each run moves about 5 MB, so it shows the patterns end to end, not production scale.

metrics.label: Upload safety
metrics.before: Folder appears at the first file

deliverables.title: Prometheus extractor and uploader
deliverables.body: A one-shot extractor in a small LXC pulls 11 PromQL queries, 15 days at 5-minute steps, as 176 raw JSON files per run, then uploads them to a Unity Catalog Volume with the Databricks SDK. A systemd unit runs it on every container start. A marker file is written last so only complete runs are treated as done.

deliverables.title: Bronze with Auto Loader
deliverables.body: Auto Loader appends raw JSON to a Delta table with an explicit schema (labels as a map), the source file and the ingest time. A checkpoint means a re-run with no new files adds zero rows.

deliverables.title: Silver in PySpark
deliverables.body: Explodes the nested response to one row per sample, keeps ten labels, builds a stable series key, drops NaN and infinite values and dedupes overlapping runs with a window function. Two runs went from 281,810 rows to 140,690. An assert fails the job if one duplicate survives.

deliverables.title: Gold with SQL stored procedures
deliverables.body: One stored procedure, refresh_gold(from_date), runs two MERGE statements into an hourly host table and a daily per-container table. Running it twice leaves the row counts unchanged.

deliverables.title: Workflow and dashboard
deliverables.body: A three-task Workflow (bronze, silver, gold) on serverless compute starts from a file-arrival trigger, so there is no schedule to maintain. An AI/BI dashboard reads gold only.

deliverables.title: Wake, run, sleep scheduler
deliverables.body: A script on the Pi checks the newest upload every 4 hours. If it is more than 10 days old it wakes the Proxmox host through my Homelab Hub, starts the container, waits for the completion marker, then stops the container and the host. It does nothing if the Databricks API doesn't answer, never toggles twice and avoids the backup window.

projects.title: Homelab Hub & Docs (open source)
projects.description: A self-hosted control panel and knowledge base for my homelab (Java 17, Spring Boot, SQLite, React): live service status, Wake-on-LAN and Proxmox power actions with typed confirmation and an audit log, a browser SSH terminal and Docker manager, plus a Docs app that publishes chosen pages through a separate read-only server. This portfolio is served that way. Interactive architecture page: https://tabtq.github.io/showcase/homelab-hub-architecture/

case.context: I wanted one place to see and control my homelab: service status, safe power actions, a terminal and somewhere to keep documentation, without exposing any of it publicly by accident. So I built a private control panel and Docs app, plus a separate read-only public side that serves only what I choose to publish. It is open source, and it runs this portfolio.

metrics.label: Automated tests
metrics.after: 800+ unit, integration and browser tests before each deploy

metrics.label: Public exposure
metrics.after: No host ports on public containers; editors on LAN and tailnet only

metrics.label: Container hardening
metrics.after: Read-only filesystems, all capabilities dropped, no-new-privileges

deliverables.title: Live service status
deliverables.body: One private dashboard for the state of the Proxmox node, its containers and the Pi's Docker services.

deliverables.title: Safe power actions
deliverables.body: Wake-on-LAN, start and stop for guests, and node shutdown or reboot. Risky actions need a typed confirmation, and every call is written to an audit log. My data-pipeline scheduler reuses these endpoints.

deliverables.title: Browser terminal and Docker manager
deliverables.body: An SSH terminal in the browser and a Docker manager for the Pi, running through a dedicated low-privilege account.

deliverables.title: Docs app with public publishing
deliverables.body: A Docs editor on its own LXC publishes chosen pages through a separate read-only server. This portfolio and the project walkthrough pages are served that way.

deliverables.title: Security- and test-first
deliverables.body: Read-only containers, dropped capabilities, private editors with no public route, and over 800 automated unit, integration and browser tests before each deploy.

homelab.name: Dual-ISP VLAN-Segmented Network
homelab.summary: A dual-ISP home network on a TP-Link ER605 gateway with bidirectional WAN failover between a 1 Gbps fiber PPPoE link and a 30 Mbps secondary ISP. VLAN 10 (high-speed) and VLAN 20 (IoT / cameras) are segmented across managed and unmanaged switches and WiFi 6 APs.
